points.t: Red, moist, sore rash **under the breasts**, in the **groin**, armpits or abdominal folds.
Skin-on-skin **friction + trapped sweat** → maceration; yeast and bacteria colonise secondarily.
**Dry and separate the folds**, barrier products, short **mild** steroid; treat confirmed candida or erythrasma.
Flexural **psoriasis**, **extramammary Paget** disease, and tinea or erythrasma treated as ‘simple intertrigo’.

cause.lead: Heat, moisture and friction in a closed fold.
points: Occluded flexure traps sweat → **maceration** → barrier failure → inflammation.
± overgrowth of resident flora: *Candida*, corynebacteria, dermatophytes, staph / strep.
**Risks**: obesity, diabetes, hyperhidrosis, immobility, incontinence, tight synthetics, hot humid weather.

visuals.caption: Inside a skin fold: two surfaces rub together, sweat is trapped, the outer layer turns white and macerated and the skin beneath becomes inflamed. Yeast and bacteria thrive in the moist crease.
visuals.alt: Cross-section of a moist macerated skin fold

features.lead: Symmetrical, moist fold redness: then look for the clue that names the cause.
points: Erythema, itch or burning, **moist macerated** skin, fissures in the crease depth.
Sites: inframammary, axillae, groin, abdominal apron, natal cleft, neck, finger and toe webs.
Infection clues: **satellite pustules** (candida), foul odour (Gram-negatives), honey crust (impetigo), **coral-red Wood’s lamp** (erythrasma).
Worked case: 3-month symmetrical inframammary rash, smooth, well-defined, **KOH negative** → irritant intertrigo.

visuals.caption: Folds where intertrigo occurs: armpits, under the breasts, the lower abdominal fold and the groin creases.
visuals.alt: Body outline with shaded skin folds

items.name: Candida
items.t: Beefy red with satellite papules / pustules.

items.name: Tinea cruris
items.t: Raised active border, central clearing; often asymmetrical.

items.name: Erythrasma
items.t: Red-brown patch, little scale or itch.

items.name: Seborrhoeic
items.t: Ill-defined salmon-pink; check scalp and face.

points: If scale, satellites or treatment failure.
Swab if pustules, crust, odour; Wood’s lamp for erythrasma.
Atypical, one fold that won’t clear, or suspected allergy.

cards.name: Inverse psoriasis
cards.clue: Shiny, well-demarcated; relapses as treatment stops.

cards.name: Extramammary Paget
cards.clue: One fold that fails to clear in an older adult: biopsy.

points: Shower after sweating; **dry folds thoroughly** (cool hairdryer).
Loose natural fibres; address incontinence and weight.
Barrier paste (zinc oxide) for weepy folds; avoid talc as the main strategy.
**Hydrocortisone 1%**, 1–2 weeks, once infection unlikely or treated.
Candida likely: topical azole (± mild steroid combo, used cautiously).
Bacterial: topical or oral antibiotic per local guidance.
Repeat mycology / culture; rethink inverse psoriasis, contact allergy, seborrhoeic dermatitis.

limits.t: Pragmatic, but reassess if no infection signs and no improvement.

items.t: Single fold that won’t clear, especially older adult: biopsy for **extramammary Paget**.
Relapses as soon as treatment stops: think **inverse psoriasis**.

pearls.t: **KOH negative ≠ never fungal**: re-test if the course is atypical.
Use a Wood’s lamp on any red-brown fold patch.

quiz.q: First step for KOH-negative irritant intertrigo?
quiz.a: Dry-care and friction reduction, plus a short course of hydrocortisone 1%.

quiz.q: Why avoid potent steroids in folds?
quiz.a: Natural occlusion increases absorption: atrophy, striae, rebound.

quiz.q: One fold that never clears in an older woman?
quiz.a: Biopsy to exclude extramammary Paget disease.
